meta.note: The letter/email task types. A task type is WHY you are writing; it fixes the register, the salutation-signoff pair and the sequence of moves. This replaces the formal/informal toggle: choosing 'Job application' already decides the register, so asking the learner a second time is redundant. Each move names the functions it draws on, resolved against ../../data/functions-corpus.json, plus any phrases specific to this task that a general function inventory has no place for. Transcribed from the FCE writing portfolio handbook. Proposal and Recommendation were dropped: they are not taught at this stage of B2. Apology and Arrangements exist in BOTH registers — the moves are identical, only the realisation changes — so each has a formal and an informal entry rather than being collapsed into one. `hasQuestions` false marks a type that is taught but has no item in the question bank yet.
meta.conventionNote: The salutation and the sign-off are a PAIR in UK convention, not two free choices. Dear Sir or Madam (recipient unknown) takes Yours faithfully; Dear Mr Silva (recipient named) takes Yours sincerely. Mixing them is the single most visible convention error in a formal B2 letter, and it is checkable rather than merely displayable — see `salutation.pairing`.

pairing.rule: Known but not intimate — regards. Safe default for a teacher, a club secretary, a colleague.
Friend or family — no fixed pair, tone matches the greeting.

salutation.teachingPoint: Portuguese has no faithfully/sincerely split, so learners treat the sign-off as free choice. Frame it as a lock: the greeting decides the ending before you have written a word.

job_application.label: Job application
job_application.recipient: An employer who advertised a post
job_application.note: The only task type where the writer is being judged as a candidate, so positive self-description is required rather than optional — and it is where Portuguese learners under-sell, because direct self-praise is less conventional in PT.

moves.label: Greeting & purpose
guide: Begin formally: Dear Sir or Madam,
State the reason for writing — applying for the advertised post
Mention where you saw the advert
phrases: I am writing with reference to your advertisement for the position of
I would like to apply for the role of … recently advertised in
I am interested in applying for the post of

moves.label: Experience & skills
guide: Describe relevant experience
Mention positive qualities — responsible, hardworking, enthusiastic
phrases: During the past few years I have been employed as
My duties have included …, which has helped me develop
I have experience working with
I consider myself as
I believe I would be a suitable candidate because
I am particularly interested in this position as it would allow me to
Furthermore, I am a motivated and reliable person who

moves.label: Request for information
guide: Ask about working hours, accommodation, salary
Clarify start and end dates if necessary

moves.label: Closing & sign-off
phrases: I very much hope you will consider my application.
I would be delighted to attend an interview at your convenience.
I look forward to hearing from you.
Thank you for considering my application.

requesting_information.label: Requesting information
requesting_information.recipient: An organisation that advertised a course, service or event
requesting_information.note: Content points map one-to-one onto questions. The organising skill is sequencing them — Firstly / Secondly / Finally — not inventing content.

moves.label: Greeting & purpose
guide: Begin formally: Dear Sir or Madam,
State the reason for writing — requesting information
Mention where you saw the advert
phrases: I am writing to enquire about
I would like to request further information regarding
I saw your advertisement for … and would like to ask

moves.label: First area of enquiry
phrases: Could you please tell me whether
I would also like to know if
Would it be possible to receive details about
I am planning to …, so I would appreciate information on
As I will be travelling with …, I would like to know whether

moves.label: Closing & sign-off
phrases: I would be grateful if you could reply at your earliest convenience.
I look forward to hearing from you soon.
Thank you very much for your assistance.

complaining.label: Complaining
complaining.note: Register discipline is the whole lesson: the complaint must stay cold. Learners reach for emotive language, which lowers Communicative Achievement rather than raising it.

moves.label: Greeting & purpose
phrases: I am writing to express my strong dissatisfaction with
I am writing with regard to
I would like to bring the following matter to your attention.

moves.label: What went wrong
phrases: Firstly, I was extremely disappointed with
Secondly, my other complaint is about
Thirdly, I was shocked to find that

moves.label: Effect on you & what you want
Closing & sign-off
phrases: I look forward to hearing from you.
I trust this matter will be dealt with promptly.
I sincerely hope that

arrangements_formal.label: Arrangements & apologies (formal)
arrangements_formal.recipient: Someone expecting you — an organiser, a host, a tutor
arrangements_formal.note: Carries bad news, so the softeners do the work. Recipient is usually named — an organiser, a tutor, a host — which makes this the ONLY formal type taking 'Yours sincerely'. Teach it against the other three formal types, where the recipient is unknown and the ending is 'Yours faithfully'. No question in the bank yet.

moves.label: Greeting & purpose
phrases: I am writing to inform you that
Due to unavoidable circumstances, I am afraid I will not be able to
I also regret to inform you that
Unfortunately,

moves.label: Closing & sign-off
phrases: I sincerely hope that
I apologise for any inconvenience caused.
I look forward to hearing from you.

reacting_to_news.label: Reacting to news
reacting_to_news.note: Split from reacting_and_inviting, which was doing double duty. Reacting to news and inviting someone share an opening move but nothing after it: this task asks about THEIR news and proposes a celebration, where an invitation describes YOUR plan. The B2 skill here is asking questions — a congratulation without curiosity reads as a card, not a letter.

moves.label: React & congratulate
guide: Congratulate them straight away
Say how the news made you feel
phrases: That's wonderful news — congratulations!
It was great to get your message!
Congratulations on your news! That's amazing!
You can't imagine how pleased I am!
I haven't stopped smiling since I read it.

moves.label: Ask about it
guide: Ask two or three real questions
Show you want the details
phrases: So tell me everything!
When do you actually start?
Have you found somewhere to live yet?
I'm dying to know whether
How are you feeling about it all?

moves.label: Suggest celebrating
guide: Propose a specific way to celebrate
Offer an alternative
phrases: We absolutely have to celebrate.
Why don't we go out for
We could always do something at mine instead.
Whatever you fancy.
Shall I organise something?

moves.label: Sign off warmly
phrases: Let me know what suits you best.
Can't wait to catch up!
So happy for you!
Talk soon!

reacting_and_inviting.label: Inviting & making plans
reacting_and_inviting.note: Reacting to a friend's news was split out into its own type: the two share an opening move and nothing after it. This one describes YOUR plan and offers practical help.

moves.label: React & say why you're writing
guide: Begin informally: Hi Alex, / Hey Sarah,
Ask how your friend is and say why you're writing
phrases: It was great to get your message!
I'm so happy to hear you're planning to visit!
That's wonderful news — I can't wait to see you!
Thanks for writing — I'm really looking forward to your trip!
You can't imagine how pleased I am that you're coming!

moves.label: Describe & recommend
phrases: There's so much to see and do here.
You should definitely visit
We could go to
I think you'd really enjoy
The best time to come is … because

moves.label: Suggest & offer
phrases: Why don't we go together to
I can show you around.
You can stay at my place if you like.
If you need help finding somewhere to stay, I can book something.
Don't worry about transport — I'll pick you up from the station.

moves.label: Sign off warmly
phrases: Let me know what dates you're thinking about.
Can't wait to catch up!
Write soon and tell me your exact dates.
Really looking forward to seeing you!
Take care and see you soon!

giving_advice.label: Giving advice to a friend
giving_advice.note: Advice must be hedged but still personal — second person is expected here, unlike in an essay. The trap is retreating into impersonal constructions, which weakens the letter.

moves.label: React to the news
phrases: Congratulations on your news! That's amazing!
I was so happy to hear about your offer!
Wow, that's brilliant — you must be really excited!
Thanks for your email — I'm so glad you told me!

moves.label: Advise & share experience
phrases: It sounds like a great opportunity!
If I were you, I'd definitely
I think you should
You ought to think about … before deciding.
From my own experience, … is really worth it.

moves.label: Offer the other side
phrases: On the other hand, you might want to consider
You could always … if you're not sure.
Have you thought about … ?

moves.label: Sign off warmly
phrases: Let me know what you decide!
I can't wait to hear how it goes.
Best of luck — I'm sure you'll make the right choice!
Keep in touch and tell me everything!

arrangements_informal.label: Making arrangements with a friend
arrangements_informal.recipient: A friend you are planning something with
arrangements_informal.note: Grammar-bearing: fixed arrangements take the present continuous in English where Portuguese would use a future. The task also requires OFFERING ALTERNATIVES — a B2 content point learners routinely skip, and one that needs the preference and suggestion language.

moves.label: Propose the plan
guide: Suggest the trip or event and a date
Keep the tone friendly
phrases: Fancy going on a day trip
Are you free next
I've got next Friday off — any chance you're free?
I'm planning a

moves.label: Outline the plan
guide: Times, travel, activity
Food and meeting place
phrases: My idea is
I was thinking
Here's what I'm thinking.
The plan is
We could meet at … around

moves.label: Offer alternatives & ask preference
guide: Give one or two alternatives
Ask what they prefer
Ask them to confirm
phrases: Does that sound good to you?
What do you reckon?
If you'd rather do something else we could
If … doesn't work we could
Just let me know what suits you best.

moves.label: Close & confirm
phrases: Hope you're up for it!
Looking forward to it!
Let me know!
Hope you can come!

apology_informal.label: Apologising to a friend
apology_informal.recipient: A friend you have let down
apology_informal.note: Apology exists in both registers and the moves are the same; only the realisation changes. The B2 skill is owning the mistake before explaining it — a brief explanation reads as an apology, a long one reads as an excuse. Worth teaching directly against arrangements_formal.

moves.label: Apologise clearly
guide: Apologise clearly and sincerely
Own the responsibility
phrases: I'm really sorry for
I owe you a massive apology for
I feel terrible about it.
I know I should have

moves.label: Explain briefly
guide: Brief explanation, not a long excuse
Acknowledge how they felt
phrases: What happened was
The thing is,
I'm not going to make excuses, but
I know that's not really an excuse.

moves.label: Make it up to them
guide: Suggest a specific plan
Offer options and stay flexible
phrases: I'd really like to make it up to you.
How about I take you out for
Can I make it up to you somehow?
Whatever you fancy is fine with me.

moves.label: Close warmly
phrases: Sorry again.
Really sorry again.
Hope you're not too upset with me.
Hope we're still okay.

thanking_visit.label: Thanking after a visit
thanking_visit.note: Pure social letter — there is no transaction to complete, so the marks live entirely in warmth and specificity. Naming one concrete moment is what separates a band 3 from a band 5.

moves.label: Thank them warmly
guide: Start warmly — Hi Emily,
Thank them and say you had a fantastic time
phrases: I just wanted to say a huge thanks for
It was great to catch up after so long.
Your family made me feel really welcome.

moves.label: What you enjoyed most
guide: Mention specific activities — meals, trips, games, conversations
Describe your favourite moment briefly
phrases: I especially enjoyed
I also loved … — we should definitely do that again.

moves.label: Compliment & appreciate
phrases: Thanks again for letting me stay.
You really went out of your way to make me feel at home.

moves.label: Future plans & sign off
phrases: Next time, you must come and visit me!
Hope everything's going well at work.
Let's plan our next weekend together soon!

questionMap.note: Maps the type keys used across the data files onto task types. THREE files use different vocabularies for the same thing — emails-questions-*.json, emails-ideas.json and emails-cards-models.json all name their types independently — so this is the single place the joins happen. Adding a synonym here is cheaper and safer than renaming keys inside the data files, and it keeps those files editable on their own terms.

cardTypes.note: emails-cards-models.json is the Model page's asset and keeps its own assembly pools — a job-application opening alone builds 224 combinations, where this file holds 14 fixed phrases. The task type therefore supplies the LABEL, the register and the salutation pair; the card file supplies the language. Two card types collapse onto one task type (Congratulate and Invite are both 'reacting and inviting'), so the Model tab row is built from the card keys and only LABELLED through the task type.
